entry_state: Acceptance requires separate evidence for engineering, accounting and scientific validity. Core conformance cases and bounded extraction, reconstruction, DSL-comparison and forecast protocols are specified without treating local demonstrations as promotion evidence. The forecast information cutoff requires exact retained versions and actual availability evidence. E1 preserves complete-package coverage and source errors; E2 tests soundness and completeness within a declared finite scope. E3 begins with operating cash flow and a joint cash/debt target; its scoring protocol continues.
exit_state: E3-E6 now distinguish predictive scores, sector data, numerical target validity and usability evidence. Budget rungs and repair rules separate invalid experiments from weak candidates. Joined sector calculations retain each validation target. Package capabilities and P0-P6 milestones specify proposed dependency order, while actual reference checks cover only parts of the design. The concrete corpus protocol continues with filing-content limitations.
findings: The CRPS display has its law, independent draws, realized amount, finite-first-moment condition and smaller-is-better orientation before it; the cited representation and two-point arithmetic follow.

Forecast scale is fixed from positive as-of assets rather than outcomes. Paired loss differences require a predeclared uncertainty design; the purposive panel alone cannot justify bootstrap inference.
Bank allowances are distinguished from realized losses; reserve validation distinguishes ultimate and one-year quantities and requires an explicit process law where simulation needs it.
The E5 normal and causal examples retain their original target meanings; passing them is not identification of a real intervention or validity on every numerical target.
The seed set101,202,303 is labeled a debugging convenience. Budget ladder and future-record requirements leave empirical promotion conditional on target-specific design.
Package and milestone tables are legible, and Chapter14 explicitly makes implementation subject to later authorization rather than treating the design sequence as execution.
